title: PSG vs Monaco: What is Happening Now
seoTitle: PSG vs Monaco: What is Happening Now
subtitle: Filipe Luís faces PSG in his first big test in France
excerpt: Former Flamengo manager Filipe Luís debuts with Monaco vs PSG this Wednesday. The Brazilian's team has a 100% record and already cleared the playoffs of.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between PSG and Monaco, scheduled for 4:05 p.m. Brasília time, takes place this Wednesday at the Parc des Princes in France. The match is the first major test for Filipe Luís, who took over at Monaco during the last transfer window and already boasts a 100% record at the start of the season.

Filipe Luís and his early success at Monaco

With two wins and just one point behind Lille, Monaco occupies second place in the French League. The Brazilian manager was praised by L’Equipe for “dominating” Olympique de Marseille and for his “defensive solidity” and “imposing ball recovery.” Eric Fronsio, a French journalist, highlighted that Filipe Luís's start to his work is very good and that he is already exciting the fans and the media.

Luis Enrique's reaction to the new manager in France

Manager Luis Enrique, who defeated Flamengo in the 2025 Intercontinental Cup final, also praised the Brazilian. He commented that Monaco is a great team and that Filipe Luís is a brave manager who likes to play football. Enrique joked about having a new competitor in France and highlighted the importance of having new coaches who value quality.

Monaco's financial and squad challenges

Monaco needs sales to balance the books. In the last window, the club sold forward Akliouche, who was bought by PSG for 50 million euros, defensive midfielder Bamba, who went to Newcastle, and left-back Caio Henrique, who went to Ajax. The club kept 22-year-old Senegalese defensive midfielder Lamine Camara, who has already become a fan favorite.

Outlook on competing against PSG

Although the expectation is to finish in the top four and secure a Champions League spot, Eric Fronsio stated that competing with PSG is impossible. Monaco has little investment and more departures than arrivals, so Filipe Luís will have to find a way to achieve big goals.

What to expect from Wednesday's clash

The clash against PSG represents a decisive test for the Brazilian manager. If Monaco can maintain the defensive solidity and offensive efficiency shown in the first matches, they could surprise this season. The match will be closely followed by fans and experts tracking the French club's development.

With information from O GLOBO.
